profile.reading:
The building at 26 Fahey Street in Stamford, Connecticut functions as a combined office and data center for what was, until May 2024, an independently operated technology company called amnet Systems. Amnet had operated since 1995, providing managed IT services, cybersecurity, colocation, cloud hosting and connectivity, and audiovisual integration services to businesses across the Northeast United States. In May 2024, Omega Systems, a larger managed service and managed security service provider, acquired amnet and folded its operations, staff, and facilities, including the Fahey Street location, into the combined company. Omega Systems describes the merged organization as a multi award winning MSP and MSSP, and the Fahey Street building continues to serve former amnet customers, who can reach 24 hour support through Omega's service desk and manage billing through Omega's customer portal, according to Omega's own announcement of the transition.

Because amnet's Stamford location was built and operated as part of a regional managed services business rather than a wholesale colocation provider, it does not carry the kind of published capacity sheet that dedicated data center operators offer. Omega Systems' own materials describe the address as an office and data center, a description that suggests a hybrid site combining staffed office space with a server and colocation room, likely sized to support amnet's existing managed services and colocation client base in the greater Stamford and lower Fairfield County market rather than to serve as a wholesale data center leasing raw capacity to outside operators. No square footage, power capacity in megawatts, cooling architecture, or Uptime Institute Tier rating is published for the building, either under the amnet name or under Omega Systems' current branding.

Stamford sits in Fairfield County, a dense corridor of corporate offices and financial services firms within commuting distance of New York City, a market where a managed services provider offering nearby colocation, rather than a hyperscale campus, fits the demand of mid sized enterprise customers who want a local partner rather than a national wholesale data center operator. The 2024 acquisition folded a long standing, regionally focused Connecticut technology company into a larger, multi state managed services platform, a consolidation pattern common across the managed IT and colocation industry as smaller regional providers combine with larger platforms backed by outside investment.

reading.body:
This Stamford facility is described by its operator as an office and data center, but no power capacity is published. Without a megawatt figure, it is not possible to assess whether this campus has material relevance to AI infrastructure scaling.

Connecticut has five mapped data center facilities, of which only two publish power capacity figures totaling 8 MW. This campus ranks third by published capacity in the state, but that ranking reflects the absence of published data rather than confirmed scale. The state context suggests most facilities in Connecticut do not disclose their specifications publicly.

To determine whether this campus matters to AI, a reader would need to contact the operator directly for power capacity, IT load density, and grid interconnection details. The published record contains none of these facts.
